offence_severity: Death penalty (minimum/maximum: not specified, but death sentence confirmed)
physical_harm: Three girls burnt alive to death and several others received burn injuries
number_of_offences: 30 accused were convicted; A-2 to A-4 were finally upheld for three counts of murder and causing burn injuries
premeditation_planning: Yes, the court found the offence was committed after previous planning and involved extreme brutality
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the evidence that A-2 to A-4 came on motorcycle, sprinkled petrol inside the bus and set it ablaze, leading to the death of three girls and burn injuries to others. The court also accepted the evidence of PW-99, PW-4, PW-5, PW-1 and PW-2, PW-8, PW-11, PW-12, PW-14, and the fact that A-4 kept the engine of the motorcycle running to escape from the scene.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses as credible, noting that their statements were corroborated by other evidence and that discrepancies in their statements did not go to the heart of the matter. The court also considered the evidence of hostile witnesses and found that relevant parts thereof could be used by the prosecution or the defence.
trial_duration: The incident occurred on 2.2.2000, the High Court judgment was confirmed on August 30, 2010, and the Supreme Court decision was on August 30, 2010.
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused and the State in the Supreme Court not stated in the judgment text.
investigation_status: Irregularities in investigation noted, but the material of earlier investigations was not relied upon by the subsequent Investigating Officer.
procedural_irregularity: Irregularities in investigation committed by the earlier I.Os. have too little relevance on the merits of the case.
appeal_history: The appeals were dismissed. The death sentences of A-2 to A-4 were confirmed. The sentences of the other accused were reduced to the period already undergone.
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused were part of a group of agitators who set ablaze a University bus full of girl-students, resulting in three girls being burnt alive and several others receiving burn injuries. The prosecution emphasized the barbaric and inhuman nature of the act, the extreme brutality, and the shock to society's collective conscience.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the prosecution's case did not warrant any trial due to contradictions in the statements of alleged eye-witnesses, the absence of a complaint by a competent officer, and the irregularities in the investigation. They also questioned the validity of the charges under Section 188 of the IPC.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the 'rarest of rare' principle, balancing aggravating and mitigating circumstances to determine the appropriateness of the death penalty.
precedent_relied_upon: Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab, AIR 1980 SC 898; Machhi Singh & Ors. v. State of Punjab, AIR 1983 SC 957; Devender Pal Singh v. State of NCT of Delhi, AIR 2002 SC 1661; and other cases cited in the judgment.
sentencing_rationale: The death sentence was imposed due to the extreme brutality, diabolical nature, and shocking impact of the crime on society. The court found that life imprisonment would be inadequate given the heinous nature of the act.
judicial_aggravating_factors: The crime was committed with extreme brutality, involved exceptional depravity, and was an unprovoked attack on helpless, innocent, young girl students. The manner of the commission of the offence was extremely brutal, diabolical, grotesque, and cruel.
other_sentence_order: The sentences of the other accused were reduced to the period already undergone, and their bail bonds were discharged.
